claims.text: Long COVID is recognized as a chronic condition; 2024 NASEM definition anchors consensus
claims.quote: This definition identifies Long COVID as an infection-associated chronic condition (IACC), specifies a minimum duration of 3 months, and expressly incorporates common symptoms and diagnosable conditions characteristic of Long COVID.

claims.text: NASEM definition requires symptoms or conditions present for at least 3 months
claims.quote: The definition requires symptoms or conditions to be present for a duration of 3 months or longer, although the timing of those 3 months is unspecified.

claims.text: committee engaged more than 1,300 participants with a focus on the patient perspective
claims.quote: The committee employed a systematic approach--engaging more than 1,300 participants—with a focus on the patient perspective and interdisciplinary dialogue.

claims.text: does not require laboratory confirmation or other proof of initial infection
claims.quote: The definition does not require laboratory confirmation or other proof of initial SARS-CoV-2 infection.

claims.text: does not list any symptom or condition as exclusionary; can be diagnosed on clinical grounds

claims.text: clinicians should recognize and monitor concerning symptoms before the 3-month mark
claims.quote: Although the definition specifies a minimum duration of 3 months to qualify as Long COVID, a clinician should recognize, acknowledge, and monitor concerning symptoms before the 3-month mark.

claims.text: definition recognizes continuous, relapsing and remitting, or progressive courses
claims.quote: Sign(s), symptom(s), or condition(s) can have variable patterns and can be continuous, relapsing and remitting, or progressive.
